class.name: VoxelMesherMarchingCubes
class.brief_description: Extracts a [VoxelField] into triangles with marching cubes.
class.description: Marching cubes walks the field one cell at a time, and for each cell places triangles according to which of its eight corners are inside the solid. Where the surface crosses a cell edge is found by interpolating between the two corner samples, so the result follows the surface more closely than the grid it was sampled on. This is the default mesher, and the one to use unless there is a specific reason not to. The surface it produces is always closed, which is what collision and volume measurement depend on. It does round off sharp creases: a corner is reconstructed as the grid saw it, so an edge finer than a voxel comes out slightly bevelled. Extraction runs on [WorkerThreadPool] across the regions a stamp touched, and output is grouped so that each material ID present in the field becomes one surface on the mesh.
